metadata.chapter_subtitle: Reading broad-band satellite images before jumping to indices

inventory.summary: The core book needed a practical image-reading bridge between the remote-sensing foundations and the existing vegetation-index chapter, so readers could learn to interpret bands before combining them into indices.
issues: There was no dedicated beginner chapter on multispectral imagery interpretation.
Readers needed help connecting spectral concepts to actual band combinations and false-colour views.
Vegetation-index work benefited from a clearer lead-in on what different bands reveal.

rewrite.summary: Added a new environmental-systems chapter that explains how multispectral bands are read, how false-colour composites work, and how to think from band response to land-surface interpretation.
editor_notes: Kept the focus on practical interpretation before moving to derived indices.
Used land-cover examples to make the bands memorable.
Positioned the chapter as the immediate precursor to vegetation-index modelling.

qa_review.summary: The chapter provides the missing interpretation step cleanly and sets up later remote-sensing modelling in a way that is accessible to first-time readers.

repair.summary: The remote-sensing modelling sequence was repaired by inserting a practical multispectral interpretation chapter ahead of vegetation indices.
actions_taken: Added a new environmental-systems chapter on multispectral imagery and band interpretation.
Inserted the chapter before vegetation indices in the book configuration and environmental-systems index.
Renumbered later environmental chapters to preserve sequence coherence.

design_review.summary: The chapter uses band-comparison visuals and reading guidance effectively, which helps learners connect colour composites to physical land-surface differences.
improvements_made: Added a beginner-facing Before You Start block.
Used a band-interpretation visual to compare visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared sensitivity.
Explained how to read false-colour imagery rather than only naming the bands.
